indications.name: Initial bariatric surgery for obesity in adults aged 18 years or older

criteria.text: Body mass index threshold, with lower thresholds for Asians when ethnicity is confirmed by provider attestation
any_of: BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² (class 2 obesity), or ≥ 27.5 kg/m² in Asians
BMI 30 to 34.9 kg/m² (class 1 obesity), or 25 to 27.4 kg/m² in Asians, with at least one clinically significant obesity-related comorbidity

criteria.text: For BMI 30 to 34.9 kg/m² (25 to 27.4 kg/m² in Asians), at least one clinically significant obesity-related comorbidity, including but not limited to these
any_of: Mechanical arthropathy in a weight-bearing joint (symptomatic degenerative joint disease)
Poorly controlled hypertension despite optimal medical management (systolic at least 140 mm Hg or diastolic 90 mm Hg or greater)
Lower extremity lymphatic or venous obstruction
Evidence of fatty liver disease, meaning metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)
Gastroesophageal reflux disease refractory to medical therapy

criteria.text: Thorough multidisciplinary evaluation within the previous 12 months includes a description of the proposed procedure or procedures
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes documentation of failure of weight loss by medical management
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes unequivocal clearance for bariatric surgery by a mental health provider
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes a nutritional evaluation by a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or registered dietician
Uses one of the covered open or laparoscopic initial procedures
any_of: Adjustable silicone gastric banding, such as LAP-BAND or REALIZE
Sleeve gastrectomy as a stand-alone or staged procedure
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb less than 150 cm
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb greater than 150 cm
Single-anastomosis duodenal-ileal bypass with sleeve gastrectomy (SADI-S), also called loop duodenal switch

indications.name: Adjustment of a silicone gastric band in adults

criteria.text: Adjustment controls the rate of weight loss or treats symptoms secondary to gastric restriction
Follows a medically necessary adjustable silicone gastric banding procedure

indications.name: Replacement of an adjustable silicone gastric band, or band removal with conversion to a second bariatric procedure, in adults

criteria.text: Evidence of band slippage or band component malfunction
The faulty component cannot be repaired
Gastrointestinal symptoms such as persistent nausea or vomiting or gastroesophageal reflux, with or without imaging evidence of obstruction

indications.name: Repair, reversal, or conversion after a major complication in adults

criteria.text: Develops a major complication from a previous bariatric surgical procedure, such as one of these
any_of: Gastroesophageal reflux disease refractory to medical therapy

criteria.text: The procedure is one of these
any_of: Conversion to a medically necessary bariatric surgical procedure

indications.name: Revision or conversion without a major complication in adults

criteria.text: Weight loss failure ≥ two years following a previous bariatric surgical procedure
Meets the initial medical necessity criteria for surgery
The requested procedure is one of these
any_of: Sleeve gastrectomy as a stand-alone or staged procedure
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb less than 150 cm
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb greater than 150 cm
Single-anastomosis duodenal-ileal bypass with sleeve gastrectomy (SADI-S), also called loop duodenal switch

indications.name: Initial bariatric surgery for morbid obesity in adolescents aged 11 to 17 years

criteria.text: Obesity threshold by BMI or percentile, whichever is lower
any_of: BMI ≥ 40 kg/m² or ≥ 140% of the 95th percentile (class 3 obesity)
BMI 35 to 39.9 kg/m² or ≥ 120% of the 95th percentile (class 2 obesity), with at least one clinically significant obesity-related comorbidity

criteria.text: For class 2 obesity, at least one clinically significant obesity-related comorbidity, including but not limited to these
any_of: Poorly controlled hypertension despite optimal medical management (systolic at least 140 mm Hg or diastolic 90 mm Hg or greater)

criteria.text: Thorough multidisciplinary evaluation within the previous 12 months includes a description of the proposed procedure or procedures
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes documentation of failure of weight loss by medical management
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes unequivocal clearance for bariatric surgery by a mental health provider
Multidisciplinary evaluation includes a nutritional evaluation by a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or registered dietician
Uses one of the covered open or laparoscopic procedures for adolescents
any_of: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb less than 150 cm
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb greater than 150 cm

criteria.text: Develops a major complication from a previous bariatric surgical procedure, such as one of these
any_of: Gastroesophageal reflux disease refractory to medical therapy

criteria.text: The procedure is one of these
any_of: Conversion to a medically necessary bariatric surgical procedure, which is Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy

indications.name: Revision or conversion without a major complication in adolescents

criteria.text: Weight loss failure ≥ two years following a previous bariatric surgical procedure
Meets the initial medical necessity criteria for surgery
The requested procedure is one of these
any_of: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb less than 150 cm
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a roux limb greater than 150 cm

exclusions: Gastric electrical stimulation (GES) or gastric pacing for the treatment of obesity
Vagus nerve stimulation for the treatment of obesity
Band over bypass
Band over sleeve
Fobi-Pouch (limiting proximal gastric pouch)
Intestinal bypass (jejunoileal bypass)
Intragastric balloon, such as Orbera, ReShape, or Obalon
Laparoscopic greater curvature plication
Mini-gastric bypass, one anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB), or loop gastric bypass

Endoscopic bariatric surgery procedures, including but not limited to NOTES, restorative obesity surgery endoluminal (ROSE), StomaphyX, duodenojejunal bypass liners such as Endobarrier, and transoral gastroplasty such as TOGA
Transoral outlet reduction (TORe)
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass combined with simultaneous gastric banding
Stomach aspiration therapy, such as AspireAssist
Vagus nerve blocking, such as Maestro
Surgical reversal, revision, or conversion for inadequate weight loss due to noncompliance with postoperative nutrition and exercise recommendations
Surgical reversal, revision, or conversion for any indication other than those listed as medically necessary
All bariatric surgical procedures for morbid obesity in an adolescent other than sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
Partial distal gastrectomy with gastroduodenostomy (CPT 43631) for reporting bariatric surgery
Partial distal gastrectomy with gastrojejunostomy (CPT 43632) for reporting bariatric surgery
Partial distal gastrectomy with formation of intestinal pouch (CPT 43634) for reporting bariatric surgery
Bariatric surgery for the primary treatment of any condition other than obesity or morbid obesity
Liver biopsy with bariatric surgery in the absence of signs or symptoms of liver disease, such as elevated liver enzymes, enlarged liver, or abnormal intraoperative findings

Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy performed concurrently with bariatric surgery to confirm a surgical anastomosis or establish anatomical landmarks, which is integral to the procedure and not separately reimbursable
documentation_requirements: Provider attestation confirming Asian ethnicity when the lower BMI thresholds for Asians are applied
A description of the proposed procedure or procedures from a multidisciplinary evaluation within the previous 12 months
Documentation of failure of weight loss by medical management
Unequivocal clearance for bariatric surgery by a mental health provider
A nutritional evaluation by a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or registered dietician
